plain_english_title: Comparing Scar Diagnostic Codes 7800–7805 Across Eras—Counting Painful Scars & Separate Ratings
what_this_means: This comparison tracks each scar Diagnostic Code (7800 through 7805) side by side across VA's 2002, 2008, and 2018 updates. It explains why older pre-October 23, 2008 rating sheets commonly show a single 10% rating even when several scars were tender, why post-October 23, 2008 decisions count every painful or unstable scar anywhere on the body, and how Diagnostic Code 7804 can combine with head/face/neck disfigurement (7800), deep scars (7801), and underlying muscle or nerve injuries.
record_clues: A post-October 23, 2008 rating decision or Disability Benefits Questionnaire (DBQ) documenting 3, 4, or 5+ painful surgical, burn, or shrapnel (SFW) scars while assigning only 10%.
Deep linear surgical or traumatic scars with underlying soft-tissue damage evaluated on or after August 13, 2018, after VA removed the 2008–2018 'nonlinear' wording restriction.
Scars that both hurt and repeatedly ulcerate or lose skin covering (which trigger an additional 10% note under post-2008 Diagnostic Code 7804).
important_cautions: When VA liberalizes a rating rule—such as the October 23, 2008 scar-count update or the August 13, 2018 linear-scar update—increased ratings based on the new rule generally cannot take effect earlier than the rule's effective date, and cannot be used to claim CUE in an earlier pre-amendment decision.
Quarantined Proposal Reminder: VA's September 29, 2025 notice (90 FR 46542) proposing changes to Diagnostic Code 7804 remains an unfinalized proposed rule and is not enacted law.
questions_for_representative: If I have multiple painful scars rated before October 2008 at 10%, would filing a current claim for an increased evaluation make sense based on today's count-based Diagnostic Code 7804 schedule?
On my post-2008 scar decision, did VA count every painful or unstable scar documented on the C&P exam—including scars already rated for disfigurement or surface area?
Did the examiner check whether any scar is both unstable (frequent skin breakdown) and painful?
